answer: An agent market selling fable editing, zephyr forecasts, and walnut pricing accepts bids only with hardware attestations. Each certified secure chip gets ten bids per day, shared across all agent keys it signs for; the ledger rejects excess bids using a stable chip identifier. Clones on one chip cannot multiply that quota: more bids require more physical chips. This assumes unforgeable chip identities; compromised manufacturer keys could enable counterfeit capacity.
